answer.short:
$x=1$ or $x=-2\pm\sqrt3$.

Let $u=x+\frac1x$; solve for $u$, then solve each resulting quadratic in $x$.
answer.worked:
$x\ne0$. Let $u=x+\frac1x$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2+2u-8&=0\\(u+4)(u-2)&=0\\u&=-4\text{ or }u=2.\end{align*}$$
For $u=2$,
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac1x&=2\\x^2-2x+1&=0\\(x-1)^2&=0\\x&=1.\end{align*}$$
For $u=-4$,
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac1x&=-4\\x^2+4x+1&=0\\(x+2)^2&=3\\x&=-2\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
All three values are nonzero.

answer.short:
$x=2\pm\sqrt3$.

Let $u=\sqrt{x+\frac1x}\ge0$, then complete the square after substituting back.
answer.worked:
The radicand is $\frac{x^2+1}{x}$, so the real domain is $x>0$. Let $u=\sqrt{x+\frac1x}\ge0$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2-u-2&=0\\(u-2)(u+1)&=0\\u&=2\text{ or }u=-1.\end{align*}$$
Reject $u=-1$.
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac1x&=4\\x^2-4x+1&=0\\(x-2)^2&=3\\x&=2\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
Both values are positive and give $4-2-2=0$ in the original equation.

answer.short:
$x=-1$.

Let $u=2^x>0$ and reject the negative root of the quadratic in $u$.

$x=-2,-\frac23,-\frac37$ or $3$.

Let $u=\left(\frac{x}{x+1}\right)^2$ and retain both square-root branches.
answer.worked:
$x\ne-1$. Let $u=\left(\frac{x}{x+1}\right)^2$.
$$\begin{align*}16u^2-73u+36&=0\\(16u-9)(u-4)&=0\\u&=\frac9{16}\text{ or }u=4\\\frac{x}{x+1}&=\pm\frac34\text{ or }\frac{x}{x+1}=\pm2.\end{align*}$$
For $\frac{x}{x+1}=\frac34$,
$$\begin{align*}4x&=3x+3\\x&=3.\end{align*}$$
For $\frac{x}{x+1}=-\frac34$,
$$\begin{align*}4x&=-3x-3\\x&=-\frac37.\end{align*}$$
For $\frac{x}{x+1}=2$,
$$\begin{align*}x&=2x+2\\x&=-2.\end{align*}$$
For $\frac{x}{x+1}=-2$,
$$\begin{align*}x&=-2x-2\\x&=-\frac23.\end{align*}$$
All four values are admissible.

answer.short:
$x=1$ or $x=4$.

Let $u=x+\frac4x$; the branch $u=-1$ gives no real roots.
answer.worked:
$x\ne0$. Let $u=x+\frac4x$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2-4u-5&=0\\(u-5)(u+1)&=0\\u&=5\text{ or }u=-1.\end{align*}$$
For $u=5$,
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac4x&=5\\x^2-5x+4&=0\\(x-1)(x-4)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }x=4.\end{align*}$$
For $u=-1$,
$$\begin{align*}x+\frac4x&=-1\\x^2+x+4&=0\\b^2-4ac&=1-16\\b^2-4ac&=-15.\end{align*}$$
This branch has no real roots. Hence $x=1$ or $x=4$.

answer.short:
$x=-1,-2$ or $2\pm\sqrt2$.

Let $u=\frac{x^2+2}{x}$; the second fraction becomes $\frac{12}{u}$.
answer.worked:
$x\ne0$, and $x^2+2>0$. Let $u=\frac{x^2+2}{x}\ne0$.
$$\begin{align*}u-\frac{12}{u}&=1\\u^2-u-12&=0\\(u-4)(u+3)&=0\\u&=4\text{ or }u=-3.\end{align*}$$
For $u=4$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2&=4x\\x^2-4x+2&=0\\(x-2)^2&=2\\x&=2\pm\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$
For $u=-3$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2+2&=-3x\\x^2+3x+2&=0\\(x+1)(x+2)&=0\\x&=-1\text{ or }x=-2.\end{align*}$$
All four values are nonzero.

answer.short:
$x=1$ or $x=\pm3$.

Let $u=\frac{x^2}{2x-3}$; the second fraction becomes $\frac{3}{u}$.
answer.worked:
$x\ne0,\frac32$. Let $u=\frac{x^2}{2x-3}\ne0$. Since $6x-9=3(2x-3)$,
$$\begin{align*}u-\frac3u-2&=0\\u^2-2u-3&=0\\(u-3)(u+1)&=0\\u&=3\text{ or }u=-1.\end{align*}$$
For $u=3$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=3(2x-3)\\x^2-6x+9&=0\\(x-3)^2&=0\\x&=3.\end{align*}$$
For $u=-1$,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=-(2x-3)\\x^2+2x-3&=0\\(x+3)(x-1)&=0\\x&=-3\text{ or }x=1.\end{align*}$$
All three values are admissible.

answer.short:
$x=\pm\sqrt2$.

Let $u=(x^2+1)^2$ and reject branches inconsistent with $x^2+1>0$.
answer.worked:
Let $u=(x^2+1)^2\ge1$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2-3u-54&=0\\(u-9)(u+6)&=0\\u&=9\text{ or }u=-6.\end{align*}$$
Reject $u=-6$.
$$\begin{align*}(x^2+1)^2&=9\\x^2+1&=\pm3.\end{align*}$$
Since $x^2+1>0$, retain only the positive branch.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+1&=3\\x^2&=2\\x&=\pm\sqrt2.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$x=\pm\frac1{27}$ or $x=\pm8$.

Let $u=x^{\frac{2}{3}}=(\sqrt[3]{x})^2>0$ and retain both signs of the cube root.
answer.worked:
$x\ne0$. Using real cube roots, let $u=x^{\frac{2}{3}}=(\sqrt[3]{x})^2>0$.
$$\begin{align*}9u+\frac4u&=37\\9u^2-37u+4&=0\\(9u-1)(u-4)&=0\\u&=\frac19\text{ or }u=4\\(\sqrt[3]{x})^2&=\frac19\text{ or }(\sqrt[3]{x})^2=4\\\sqrt[3]{x}&=\pm\frac13\text{ or }\sqrt[3]{x}=\pm2\\x&=\pm\frac1{27}\text{ or }x=\pm8.\end{align*}$$
All four values are nonzero and give $9u+\frac{4}{u}=37$.

answer.short:
$x=2$.

Let $u=\sqrt{x-2}\ge0$ and reject the negative substitute root.
answer.worked:
$x\ge2$. Let $u=\sqrt{x-2}\ge0$, so $x=u^2+2$.
$$\begin{align*}u^2+2+u-2&=0\\u^2+u&=0\\u(u+1)&=0\\u&=0\text{ or }u=-1.\end{align*}$$
Reject $u=-1$. Thus $u=0$ and $x=2$. Check: $2+\sqrt{2-2}-2=0$.
